list: The official 55 trophies: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze, 28 hidden on PSN. Names, descriptions and grades are as PlayStation publishes them, as listed by PSNProfiles and Exophase. Progress targets are the counts PlayStation tracks, as published by PSNProfiles.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum is the ledger itself: it unlocks on its own the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing separate to hunt. Work the roadmap in order, keep an eye on the one possibly missable entry in Stage 4, and use the 100% completion trophy in this stage as your final checklist. When the last bronze, silver or gold pops, this one follows immediately.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: A story trophy for finishing Gone Fishing, the opening mission named in the official description. Simply start the game and play the introduction through to its end; the trophy pops as the mission completes. It cannot be missed, because the story cannot advance without it.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Play through the whole of Chapter 1 and this pops when the chapter closes. Before you leave Chapter 1 behind, a word of caution from the missable flag elsewhere in this ledger: other guides report that the first meditation spot for Positive Mental Attitude is offered during this chapter and becomes unavailable afterwards, so take that moment when it is offered rather than pressing on.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission of Chapter 2 and the trophy lands as the chapter ends. The name is shown exactly as PlayStation publishes it, asterisks included. Nothing optional is required and nothing here can be missed: chapter trophies are the spine of the story and unlock in sequence.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Complete Chapter 3 from its first mission to its last. By this point both protagonists and the wider map are in play, so it is a good moment to start the side strands and collectibles in the later roadmap stages alongside the story rather than leaving everything to the end. The chapter trophy itself is unmissable.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4 to earn this one. Keep a manual save at the start of the chapter as a general safety net, a habit other guides recommend for the whole run, then simply play the chapter through. Like every chapter trophy, it is awarded for story progress and cannot be skipped or missed.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: The gold for finishing the final mission of the story. Play the campaign to its conclusion and it pops as the last mission ends. Before starting the finale, tidy up anything chapter-bound you still owe, and keep a manual save from before the point of no return so the post-story cleanup in the later stages starts from a save you trust.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run, named in the official description. It arrives as part of the campaign, so following the story markers is the whole method: finish the mission and the trophy is yours. It is tied to a required mission and cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish The Cartel Heist, the set-piece mission named in the official description, reached by following the main story. Heists in this series reward a moment of preparation, so go in stocked and follow the mission objectives through to the escape; the trophy pops on completion and cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play when the campaign offers it. There is no optional condition attached in the official description: play the mission from start to finish and the trophy unlocks with it. Story missions are mandatory, so this one cannot be missed.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the story mission Headliners. It is one of the named campaign missions in the official list, so progress through the story until it appears, complete its objectives, and the trophy follows. Nothing in the description suggests an optional or missable condition.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete VCIA Takedown, the airport-authority mission named in the official description (VCIA is the airport that also appears in Catch Me If You Can). Play it as the story presents it and finish every objective; the trophy unlocks on completion and, as a required story mission, cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish Operation Savage Glory, the named story mission in the official description. Follow the campaign until the operation begins, complete it, and the trophy is awarded. It belongs to the mandatory story path in Stage 1 of the roadmap, so it cannot be missed.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: The long gold: raise the in-game completion statistic to 100%. Treat the rest of this ledger as its checklist, because story, side strands, activities, collectibles and challenges all feed the percentage. Work it last, in Stage 7, using the in-game completion counter to find what is still outstanding, and expect it to be the final gold most players earn before the platinum.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts, the target PlayStation tracks for this silver. Stunts are a repeatable open-world activity, so build the habit early: take the jumps and stunt opportunities the world offers as you travel between missions instead of fast-travelling past them, and keep the counter in this tracker updated. Anything left over is a Stage 3 grind with the whole map open, and none of it is missable.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Sample every type of activity the game offers, once each: PlayStation tracks 9 activity types. You do not need to win or master any of them for this trophy, only to try them, so as each new activity unlocks during the story, play it a single time and tick it off. It pairs naturally with the rest of Stage 3 and cannot be missed.

sources.label: PSNProfiles trophy list (PSN target: 9 activity types)

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge: PlayStation tracks 42 of them. Work through the range weapon by weapon, learn each challenge’s scoring rhythm, and replay a challenge immediately while its layout is fresh rather than moving on with a silver or bronze. Accuracy streaks matter more than raw speed in most range formats, so slow down first and speed up once the targets feel routine. The range stays available, so this silver is never missable, just methodical.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at every location: PlayStation tracks 14 locations. A win is required, not just a finish, so learn each course with a practice run, then race it clean; one mistake usually costs more time than a cautious line. Tick locations off in this tracker as you clear them so the last few are easy to find. Races remain available all game, so nothing here is missable.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races. The word different is the catch: repeating one easy race twenty times does not advance the counter, so spread your wins across the race calendar and track which ones you have actually won. Bring a competitive vehicle for each class, and if a race keeps beating you, return later with better wheels rather than grinding it frustrated. Races are repeatable, so this cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Fishing is one of the activity types counted by Master of None, and Cal is its named rival in the official description: find the fishing challenge, learn the reeling rhythm on ordinary catches first, then take Cal on. If he wins a round, challenge him again; the trophy only needs one victory and the challenge can be retried, so it is not missable.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game, start to finish. Any cabinet counts as far as the official description says, so pick the game that suits you, learn its pattern, and see it through to its end rather than walking away mid-run. It is one of the quickest bronzes in Stage 3 and a natural tick while sampling activities for Master of None. Arcade games stay available, so it cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy’s strand of side missions, ending with his final mission. Stranger strands unfold over several meetings, so start Andy’s chain when it first appears and return whenever a new episode unlocks instead of leaving the whole strand to the endgame. The trophy pops when his last mission completes. Other guides note that side strands can be tied to story progress, so beginning them early is the safe habit, though only Positive Mental Attitude is flagged as possibly missable in this ledger.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton’s mission strand through to his final mission. Work each episode as it unlocks; strands like this one count toward the eight strands needed for Strangers & Freaks as well, so progress here does double duty. The trophy unlocks when Kenton’s last mission ends. Start the strand when you meet him rather than postponing it, the same early-start habit recommended for every Stage 2 strand.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: See Billy’s strand through to his final mission and complete it. As with the other named characters in Stage 2, his missions arrive in stages across the game, so check back with him as the story advances and finish each new episode when it appears. Completing his finale also moves the Strangers & Freaks counter. The trophy pops on completion of that last mission.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 full mission strands for strangers across Leonida, the silver that organises Stage 2. A strand means a character’s whole chain, not a single mission: Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone each have a finale trophy of their own in this stage, and finishing strands like theirs is how the counter climbs. Start every strand when it appears, keep the counter updated here, and chase the last strands once the story is done if any remain.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy’s strand by completing his final mission. Follow his episodes as they unlock through the game and the trophy lands at the end of the last one. His strand is one of the eight counted toward Strangers & Freaks, so completing it advances two trophies at once. Begin it when Randy first appears, in line with the early-start approach for all side strands.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete Tyrone’s final mission to close out his strand. Play his episodes in order as the game offers them, and expect the finale only after the earlier ones are done. The trophy pops at the end of that last mission, and the finished strand also counts toward the eight needed for Strangers & Freaks. Start early and revisit him as the story moves on.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every meditation spot across Leonida: PlayStation tracks 18 spots, and this tracker counts them as you find each one. POSSIBLY MISSABLE: this is the one trophy other guides flag as potentially missable. The first meditation spot is offered at home in Chapter 1 and is reported to become unavailable after that chapter, so meditate there the first time it is offered and do not put it off. Later spots need both protagonists playable together, which opens up as the story advances. Do every spot the moment it appears and keep a manual save at the start of each chapter as a safety net. That missable warning is an inference reported by other guides, not a confirmed fact from the official description, and this guide labels it that way on purpose.

sources.label: GTA Zone trophy list (missable warning as reported by PowerPyx)

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal Bret asks for. Bret’s request belongs to the side content of Stage 2: take the job when he offers it, track the animal the way the mission directs, and complete the hunt. A unique animal means one specific quarry rather than any animal of its kind, so follow Bret’s brief instead of hunting at random. The trophy pops when the hunt is delivered.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 full collectible card sets. A set only counts when every card in it is found, so three finished sets beat a drawer full of partial ones: concentrate on completing one set at a time and use this tracker to note which sets are closest to done. Cards are hidden around Leonida, so search buildings and landmarks thoroughly as the story takes you through each area. Collectibles remain available after the story, so this silver is not missable.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK action at 100 different locations, the target PlayStation tracks. Locations are the point: repeating it in one place does not build the counter, so make it a travel habit and do it somewhere new in every area you visit, keeping the counter here up to date. Paired with The Goodtime State’s full exploration of Leonida, the 100 accumulate naturally across Stage 4. It stays available all game and cannot be missed.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges of any kind. Challenges sit underneath the activities in Stage 3, so the efficient route is variety: as you work through races, ranges and other activities, accept the challenges attached to them rather than hunting challenges in isolation. Keep the counter updated here; if you fall short late in the run, the remaining challenges can be mopped up with the full map open. Nothing about them is missable.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner beside you, raise a 4-star wanted level, then lose it completely and escape. Both halves matter: the stars must reach four while you are together, and the escape only counts once the heat is fully gone, so break line of sight, keep moving, and change vehicles if the pursuit tightens. Do it deliberately in free roam rather than hoping it happens during a mission, and it can be retried as often as needed.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, without your wanted level dropping away between them. Plan a small circuit of shops close together before you start, rob the first, and move straight to the next while the heat is still on you; dawdling until the stars fade resets the chain. Your partner must be with you throughout, so set this up in free roam when you are together. Failed chains cost nothing but time, so retry until it flows.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles, the target PlayStation tracks. Discovery is about variety, so get into vehicles you have never used before whenever you see one parked or passing, across every class and neighbourhood; the vehicles around wealthy districts, worksites and the countryside differ a lot. It pairs well with On the Spot’s vehicle registering in Stage 7. Keep the counter updated here and the total builds steadily through normal play.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies inside one single use of Combat Focus, the ability named in the official description. The trick is preparation: do not trigger it on the first enemy you see. Wait for a group of at least five, line them up, then activate it and work through them before it expires. Mission firefights and gang operations in Stage 5 offer dense groups if free roam does not. A failed attempt costs nothing; try again at the next crowd.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport that also hosts the VCIA Takedown story mission. In plain terms, the official description points at leaving the airport in a way the airport did not schedule: get yourself airside, take an aircraft that was never cleared for you, and get airborne. Expect a wanted level for it, so plan the escape as part of the attempt. It is a free-roam stunt and can be retried, so it is not missable.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: The official description is a joke with a vehicle name inside it: Rhinos are tanks, and it gets hot inside them. Read plainly, this is the tank trophy: get into a Rhino when the game puts one in front of you, whether that is during a story set-piece or by taking one in free roam, and spend time at its controls. The description gives no count or condition beyond the Rhino itself, so this guide claims no more than that; if a military response brings one to you, that is your moment.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store and get through it without being detected. Stealth is the whole requirement, the opposite of the noisy shop chain in Retail Therapy: scout the store first, move quietly, avoid raising an alarm, and leave before anyone knows. If you are spotted, walk away and set up a fresh attempt rather than finishing loudly; the trophy needs one clean robbery, and attempts are unlimited.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape after each one, the silver at the heart of Stage 5. A vault only counts when you get away, so plan the exit before the entrance: vehicle placed, route in mind, and enough firepower or stealth for whichever approach the bank allows. Spread the robberies out as banks become available and track them here. Each escape finishes one fifth of the trophy, and failed attempts can simply be retried.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the take. Watch for one on its route in free roam, stop it, get its cargo, and then lose the response that follows; the trophy needs the escape as well as the robbery, so have a fast vehicle and an exit route ready before you make your move. Armored trucks keep appearing, so a botched attempt is only a delay, never a miss.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all of Leonida: PlayStation tracks 52 areas. Work the map systematically, region by region, and let the other Stage 4 hunts carry you into corners you would otherwise skip: card sets, meditation spots and WAiNK locations all reward detours. Any grey patch left at the end is a short road trip with the whole game open. Exploration is permanent once done and cannot be missed.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang: PlayStation tracks 9 gangs. One robbery per gang is the requirement, so variety matters more than volume; when you hit an operation, note here which gang it belonged to, because repeating the same gang does not advance the counter. As new territories and gangs reveal themselves through the story, clear their operation once and move on. Operations remain available, so this is a Stage 5 sweep, not a missable.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach, exactly as the official description says. This is one of the quiet moment trophies gathered in Stage 6: go to Ocean Beach, order or take the cocktail where the game offers it, and take in the view rather than rushing off. The description names the place and the act and nothing more, so this guide claims nothing more; if the moment is offered during a visit or a mission, accept it instead of postponing it.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style. The official description describes an exit, not an entrance: get into a vehicle inside a showroom and drive it out through the glass rather than using the door. It is a deliberate one-off moment in Stage 6, so when you find yourself in a showroom with a car at hand, take the loud way out. Showrooms stay where they are, so the moment can be set up again if you miss the chance.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley, the venue named in the official description. Go to that alley and bowl: the trophy is tied to playing there, so a game at any other alley would not be the one described. Bowling also counts among the activities sampled for Master of None, so this visit does double duty. The alley is a permanent location, and the moment is not missable.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description, a partnership with mass appeal, is deliberately vague, and the honest reading is that this is a story moment between the two protagonists that the game stages for you rather than a feat you set up. Play the story with both partners together, take the joint activities and moments the game offers the pair, and expect it to arrive as part of that partnership. This guide claims no specific step the description does not support; it is grouped in Stage 6 with the other one-off moments so you check it during cleanup before assuming it is outstanding.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices, for better or worse: PlayStation tracks a count that runs to 500. This is a long-horizon counter rather than a single feat, so the method is simply to keep playing and keep choosing: take the optional interactions, decisions and responses the game offers instead of skipping past them, and watch the counter climb in this tracker. If it is short near the end of the run, ordinary open-world play in Stage 6 cleanup is what feeds it. Nothing in the description suggests a deadline, so treat it as cumulative, not missable.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time’s the charm, says the official description, and that is genuinely all it says. The plain reading is a retry trophy: something in the game is failed, or goes wrong, and then succeeds on the second attempt. When the game offers you a second try at something, take it rather than reloading an earlier save to protect a perfect record. This guide deliberately invents no specific event, because the description names none; check this one during Stage 6 cleanup, by which time most players will have retried something.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: What the hell just happened? is the whole official description, which marks this as the game’s strange-encounter trophy: something odd is out there in Leonida, and witnessing it is the requirement. Explore off the main roads, especially while completing The Goodtime State’s 52 areas, and when the game presents something that makes no sense, stay and watch it play out instead of driving away. No location is named in the description, so this guide points at no invented spot; it sits in Stage 6, the odd-moments stage, where it belongs.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl ’em over with a melee drive-by: strike a pedestrian-style target with a melee attack delivered from a moving vehicle, as the official description’s bowling joke describes. Set it up in a quiet street rather than in traffic chaos: roll slowly past your target, swing as you pass, and let the vehicle’s motion carry the hit. It is a technique trophy, so a few practice passes are normal, and it can be attempted whenever you are driving, which makes it a Stage 6 cleanup item rather than a missable.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Marked bills come from the crime work in Stage 5, so this Stage 7 money trophy is where that income is washed clean: whenever you are holding marked bills, route them through your contacts instead of sitting on them, and keep the running total updated here. It is cumulative across the whole run, so steady laundering after every robbery finishes it without a dedicated grind.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops, in total. The words across all shops mean the spending is cumulative everywhere, not $100,000 in one place, so ordinary play does most of the work: vehicles, clothing, weapons and supplies all count toward the same pot. If you are short late in the run, Stage 7 is the time to stop hoarding and buy the expensive things you have been eyeing. Keep the total updated here and the trophy pops when the counter crosses the line.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase every garage property: PlayStation tracks 8 garages. This is a money trophy in the truest sense, because the only obstacle is price, so it belongs in Stage 7 once story and crime income has filled your pockets. Buy them as they become affordable rather than saving for all eight at once, since owned garages are useful along the way, and tick each purchase off here. Properties stay on sale, so it cannot be missed, only postponed.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app, the service named in the official description. Whenever you acquire a vehicle you intend to keep, register it in the app there and then instead of meaning to do it later; ten registrations accumulate quickly once it becomes a habit. It pairs naturally with Whip It Good’s 100 discovered vehicles: vehicles you find in Stage 4 are candidates to register here in Stage 7. The counter in this tracker keeps the running total honest.
